acceptance_criteria.description: TcpListener::bind is bounded and reports timeout without leaving a listener task.
Graceful shutdown timeout deterministically aborts and boundedly joins the retained task; no JoinHandle is dropped while its server may still run.
The movement path proves exactly one ordered peer update rather than only at least one update.

The full two-WebSocket behavior and teardown assertions still pass, and focused/full phase2_http tests, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass with only the owned test file changed from the sealed candidate.

closed_decisions: Preserve the accepted two-account authentication, lease, ticket, reciprocal spawn, ordered update, and disconnected-despawn assertions exactly.
Wrap OS-selected loopback TcpListener binding in an existing bounded test timeout and return a stable test error on expiry.

Shutdown must retain ownership of the JoinHandle through the timeout decision; if graceful completion times out, abort the task and await the aborted handle under a second finite cleanup bound so it cannot detach.
Drop remains a final defensive abort path only and must not replace the explicitly awaited normal shutdown path.
After consuming the expected ordered movement update, prove the receiving peer has no duplicate or out-of-order update before initiating disconnect.
All changes remain test-only in phase2_http.rs.
forbidden_changes: Do not change production code, authentication, tickets, realtime/presence behavior, assertion coverage, timeout constants globally, Cargo files, other tests, documentation, or orchestration state.
Do not detach or leak a server task after any timeout, add unbounded waits, use a fixed port, log credentials, or weaken teardown errors.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert another worker's edits.
objective: Correct the three confirmed lifecycle and exact-update findings in the two-WebSocket presence acceptance test without changing its authenticated behavior or production code.

return_when: All three confirmed P2 findings are resolved and verification outcomes are recorded.
A safe bounded fix requires a production or out-of-scope change.
A concrete toolchain or isolated-worktree failure prevents progress within the execution budget.
